He teaches and consults in the areas of business ethics and corporate governance. He is the co-founder of IntegrityIQ, a Trinity Campus Company supported by Enterprise Ireland. He is the author of “Power and Corporate Responsibility”, the joint winner of the 2024 Academy of Management’s Social Issues in Management Best Book Award. He is the recipient of the Trinity Business School Research Excellence Award – Best Managerial Impact (2025) and has received annual Teaching Excellence Awards from Trinity Business School from 2023 to 2026. He is an associate professor extraordinaire at Stellenbosch Business School in South Africa, and a former visiting scholar at the Wharton School (University of Pennsylvania) and the Mendoza College of Business (University of Notre Dame). He was the co-chair of the Business 20 (B20) Task Force on Integrity and Compliance (2022 and 2020), is a former member of the Global Future Council on Transparency and Anti-Corruption of the World Economic Forum (2019 – 2022) and is the regional partner for Africa and Ireland at the International Board Foundation in St Gallen, Switzerland. He is a former associate director of KPMG Forensic Accounting, where he was the regional service specialist for ethics and integrity services in the Europe, Middle East and Africa region. He holds a PhD in Business Administration, a Masters degree in Philosophy (cum laude) as well as a Masters degree in Business Administration (MBA), all from Stellenbosch University in South Africa.

David Luna:
Workshop Coordinator for PPPs Critical to Fight Organized Crime and Threat Networks Fueling Global Corruption and Insecurity (4.1)

David M. Luna is the Executive Director of the International Coalition Against Illicit Economies (ICAIE) / ICAIE Foundation, and co-Founder of the Illicit Shadows LLC’s media and digital series on the Dark Forces Shaping the Global Criminal Underworld. A former U.S. diplomat and national security official, Mr. Luna is a globally-recognized strategic thought leader and leading voice on international relations, geopolitical risks, criminal-threat convergence, corruption, organized crime, terrorism, hubs of illicit trade, threat finance, the changing character of war (gray zones), and global illicit economies that fuel greater insecurity and instability around the world.

For over 20 years, as a U.S. Government official, Mr. Luna partnered with 150+ member states in numerous international organizations, diplomatic fora/initiatives and public-private partnerships to promote the U.S. foreign policy goals and national security anti-crime priorities of the President of the United States and Secretary of State over four successive Administrations.  In addition to chairing numerous working groups across the diplomatic world, Mr. Luna held senior positions with the U.S. Department of State, Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs (INL), including directorships for national security, transnational crime, and anti-corruption and good governance; and advisor to the Secretary’s Coordinator for the Rule of Law. Mr. Luna also served as an Assistant Counsel to the President, Office of the Counsel to the President, The White House; and other positions with the U.S. Department of Labor and U.S. Senate.

Mr. Luna previously also served as the President of the OECD Task Force on Countering Illicit Trade and Chair of both the Business at OECD (BIAC) and U.S. Council for International Business (USCIB) anti-illicit trade committees; Vice Chair of the World Economic Forum’s Global Agenda Council on Illicit Trade and Organized Crime, Chair, APEC Anti-Corruption and Transparency (ACT) Working Group; Chair of the U.S.-China Anti-Corruption Working Group of the Joint Law Enforcement Liaison Group and in other leadership positions in the G7, and other diplomatic fora and public-private partnerships on anti-crime and global security; and Chair of the Summit for Democracy (S4D) Kleptocracy and Illicit Finance Working Group -- a civil society-driven dialogue to fight corruption and money laundering to defend democracy against authoritarianism.

Mr. Luna is a Senior Fellow for National Security with the Terrorism, Transnational Crime, and Corruption Center (TraCCC); a graduate (M.S.S.) of the U.S. Army War College, and received his B.A. from the University of Pennsylvania, J.D. from The Columbus School of Law, The Catholic University of America, and awarded numerous certificates from the Harvard Business School (HBS).
David Meyer:
David Meyer is President of the Council of Europe’s Group of States against Corruption (GRECO). He was elected in November 2024 and took office in January 2025. He has more than a decade of experience with GRECO. He has headed the United Kingdom Delegation since 2014 and has been an elected member of GRECO’s Bureau since 2016.

David has worked on every part of GRECO’s work. He has served as an evaluator and rapporteur and has led high-level missions to member states focused on addressing non-compliance with GRECO’s recommendations. He also contributed to the development of GRECO’s Fifth and Sixth evaluation rounds as a member of the respective working groups.

A career civil servant, David leads the UK Ministry of Justice’s work on international engagement, the rule of law and the overseas territories. His extensive experience spans international policy, criminal justice, and constitutional matters, reflecting his commitment to promoting transparency and good governance on both national and international stages.

Diana Chigas: Diana Chigas is Co-Director of the Corruption, Justice and Legitimacy Program (CJL) at Besa Global, which has pioneered the use of systems thinking in corruption analysis and the role of social norms as drivers of corruption and obstacles to anti-corruption efforts. She is also a Professor of the Practice of International Negotiation and Conflict Resolution at the Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy at Tufts University (United States). Diana has led the work CJL has done to date on the intersection of gender norms and social norms in corruption and anti-corruption and on corruption and anti-corruption in conflict contexts. Diana has over 30 years’ experience as a facilitator and consultant in negotiation and conflict resolution, including working with inter-governmental organizations, governments and civil society on preventive diplomacy and peacemaking and inter-group dialogue. Diana has a JD from Harvard Law School and MALD from the Fletcher School at Tufts University.
Dolores Calvo:
Dolores is part of the steering group for Uppsala University Research Environment on Sexual Corruption (UURESC), where she co-developed the conceptual framework on sexual corruption that much of the field now builds on, and coordinates research on legal frameworks and reporting mechanisms. She has also developed and delivered applied resources, including policy briefs, workshops, and online courses on sexual corruption. Dolores is also a member of the Sexual Corruption taskforce, Working Group on Gender, Inclusion & Corruption, Global Civil Society Coalition for the UNCAC.

Dolores will speak about a forthcoming Toolkit on Sexual Corruption, which translates research and legal analysis into a practical framework that institutions can use to move from recognising and naming the harm to preventing and addressing it. The toolkit is being developed through broad global collaboration among experts, practitioners, and researchers, including UU-RESC, the U4 Anti-Corruption Resource Centre, the Global Civil Society Coalition for the UNCAC, and Transparency International, in consultation with UNODC and Sida. The presentation will also introduce the Sexual Corruption Legal Mapping and Database, which provides the legal foundation and first step towards the toolkit. The mapping and database show how sexual corruption is recognised and/or regulated across different jurisdictions around the world, making legislative gaps visible. The database serves as a global resource for governments, civil society, activists, and legal practitioners working to strengthen legal frameworks, advance the goals of Resolution 10/10, and support action against sexual corruption. The database has been developed through a collaboration between UURESC, the Global Civil Society Coalition for the UNCAC, and the International Lawyers Project, in partnership with the global law firm Hogan Lovells Cadwalader.

Elizabeth Andersen:
Elizabeth “Betsy” Andersen is the Executive Director of the Basel Institute on Governance, where she leads the Institute’s strategic direction and oversees its global efforts to counter corruption, strengthen governance and promote integrity in the public and private sectors. She assumed the role in March 2025, following a distinguished career at the intersection of law, justice, governance and international development.

Before joining the Institute, Betsy served as Executive Director of the World Justice Project, a non-profit organisation working internationally to advance the rule of law.

Betsy has a rich legal background spanning academia and practice. Among other roles, she has served as Associate Executive Director of the American Bar Association and Director of its Rule of Law Initiative. She has also served as Executive Director of both the American Society of International Law and Human Rights Watch’s Europe and Central Asia Division.

She is a frequent speaker and widely published author on topics relating to international human rights, transitional justice and rule of law development, and she has served as an adjunct professor at the American University Washington College of Law.

Betsy brings extensive experience working with and serving on the advisory committees and boards of non-profit organisations and associations, including the International Law Institute (U.S.), CEELI Institute (Czech Republic), Misongi (Cameroon) and the ASIL Women in International Law Interest Group (U.S.). She is a member of the American Law Institute and Council on Foreign Relations and currently serves as Chair of the Board of Trustees of Williams College.

For her contributions to advancing the rule of law and international justice, Betsy has been honoured with numerous awards. These include a Williams College Bicentennial Medal, the American Society of International Law Prominent Woman in International Law Award, and the American Bar Association Section of International Law World Order Under Law Award.

She holds a Bachelor of Arts (BA) in History and Russian Studies from Williams College, a Master in Public Affairs (MPA) from Princeton University’s School of Public and International Affairs, and a Juris Doctor (JD) from Yale Law School.

Faith Doherty:
Faith Doherty leads the Forests Programme at the Environmental Investigation Agency (EIA) UK. She has worked on environmental crime, forest governance and human rights for more than three decades, with extensive experience across Southeast Asia and international timber and commodity markets.

Since joining EIA in the late 1990s, Faith has led investigations and campaigns exposing illegal logging, corruption and the criminal networks and corporate interests driving forest loss. Working closely with civil society organisations and independent forest monitors, particularly in Indonesia and Myanmar, she has helped expose the links between corruption, weak governance, illegal timber trade and threats to forest-dependent communities.

Faith played a leading role in EIA’s work to secure stronger European measures against illegal timber, including the EU Timber Regulation, and in efforts to improve transparency and accountability within timber supply chains and forest governance.

Her work increasingly examines the convergence of environmental crime, corruption and illicit finance, including forest destruction associated with agricultural commodities and mining. She also works to strengthen the use of international anti-corruption and organised crime frameworks, including UNCAC and UNTOC, to address environmental crime and the corruption and financial systems that enable it. Evidence generated through EIA investigations is used to support governments, enforcement agencies, civil society and communities, inform policy reform and corporate accountability, and strengthen international action against environmental crime.
Ferdian Yazid:

François Valérian:
François Valérian comes from France. He is the Chair of Transparency International. He has been working to make finances more transparent over the last decade through his work and teachings.

François Valérian was elected Chair of the Transparency International Board of Directors in 2023. Since 2019 he had been a member of the International Board where he was active in various committtees, including the Membership Accreditation Committee, which he chaired until 2022. From 2013 to 2023 he was a member of the board of Transparency International France, where he worked on illicit financial flows, political integrity and strategic litigation. Formerly the leader of business integrity programmes at the Transparency International Secretariat, François initiated Transparency International’s advocacy at the G20 around financial regulation and anti-corruption.
